l2_capacity_transition.note: three bf16 streams put the working set at 25 MB at 4194304 elements and 50 MB at 8388608, crossing A800's 40 MB L2; the step between those two samples is that capacity crossing, a hardware fact rather than a chosen breakpoint

lookup_rule_note: step_down_largest_sampled_element_not_exceeding_request; the measured curve is monotone non-decreasing in elements, so the value at the largest sampled size at or below the request is a lower bound on the request's own task time, and no interpolation shape is chosen

probe_launch_geometry.note: read from the CUPTI trace as discrete launch facts; no duration was consumed. Production A800 elementwise launches the same template at the same geometry, so the floor transfers without crossing geometries

warm_probe_caveat: the probe replays the same tensors, so mid-size samples are L2-warm while production elementwise reads are colder. A warm measurement is faster than a cold one, so this curve is a conservative lower bound on production task time, which is the direction a floor requires; it must not be read as a prediction of production duration
